verdicts.strongest_argument: I concede the narrow point - the corpus never connects these filings to the print, and initial 13Gs really are among the least-covered ownership events - but the claim as written is broken by how the form works, and by the tape it cites. A Schedule 13G initial filing carries a position as of an event date that precedes it: a qualified institution files within 45 days of the quarter-end in which it crossed 5%, so a 13G accepted 2026-07-30 most plausibly describes a holding as of 2026-06-30, not one built 'while the stock traded in the $90s'. The finding infers a purchase window from a filing date, which is exactly the stale-document pattern - the snapshot makes it look current when the underlying fact is a month or more old. Second, 13G rather than 13D is the passive box; two new 5% holders at a December-2024 IPO whose float is mechanically expanding through lockup release is the ordinary consequence of index and passive managers tracking a growing free float, which is structural, not conviction, and it is the mirror image of the supply the hunter's own second finding documents. Third, the price argument runs the wrong way: the finding says the 98.04-to-81.58 five-session collapse proves the 13Gs were not priced, but a -16.8% air pocket into a print is a tape rejecting the name, and the fact that no captured item explains it is a capture limitation, not evidence about what institutions were doing. The corroborating half - Cowen $125, Morgan Stanley $124/$115, Piper $115, BTIG and Truist $110, BMO $103, Baird $94, Freedom $155, KeyBanc and Needham $125, consensus $104 - is fully published in docs/, dated 2026-06-10 through 2026-07-03, and the hunter concedes it is two to three months stale; stale targets sitting above spot is the normal state of a de-rating growth name, not information.

Neither 13G date shows a volume signature: I could not isolate 07-30 or 08-06 as unusual sessions. run_up_5d_pct -16.79% and 31.8% off the 52-week high mean the run-in is emphatically negative, and using that fall as proof the accumulation is unpriced is the inversion this role exists to block.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: The 13G bodies naming the filers, the share counts and the event dates - if either is a fundamental manager with an event date in late July at $90-plus rather than a passive institution as of 30 June, the claim becomes real.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is structural and known in the strictest sense: insider sale filings stop before an earnings release at every company with a trading policy, so 'the cadence stopped on 2026-08-17, three weeks before the print' describes the blackout calendar rather than anything about ServiceTitan. The finding concedes the two decisive points itself - 'Individual Form 4s are the most-aggregated filing there is, so I am claiming very little here', and that this is 'a December 2024 IPO still working through lockup-expiry distribution', i.e. the overhang is the single most widely understood feature of a nine-month-old IPO. The chart evidence it offers is also published rather than derived: the same digest calls the level a 'triple top' on 2026-07-22 and a 'quadruple top' on 2026-07-28, so the failure at $100 was named by the holder base in real time before the 08-27 retest at 100.64 and the full retrace. And the claim is explicitly a cap on TTAN#0's magnitude rather than an independent edge, drawn from the same file, which the hunter says should collapse the two into one source cluster. Mechanically, the return of supply after the window reopens resolves after 8 September, so it does not land inside this print's reaction at all.

interactions: The two findings rest on the same file, filings.json, and point in opposite directions - accumulation versus distribution - which the hunter states outright and does not resolve. They cannot both carry weight: TTAN#1's lockup-distribution frame is the most likely benign explanation for the passive 5% crossings in TTAN#0 (an expanding free float pulls in index and passive holders), so the second finding partly explains away the first rather than capping it.
corpus_limits: No 13G, Form 4 or Form 144 bodies are stored, so I could not read the filers, share counts or event dates - the single fact that would decide TTAN#0. The news channel ran zero queries across all eleven sweeps for TTAN, so there is no wire copy, no preview and no consensus in the capture, and in particular nothing explains the 08-27 +9.1% spike or the -16.6% unwind into the print; that silence is a capture artefact and I have treated it as neither concession nor publication. No option chain. No tripwire-flagged documents excluded.
